issues.title: Test-quality enforced in the reviewer (extends CAM-56 Layer B): anti-mock + per-test discipline + flaky
issues.description: Extends the CAM-56 reviewer Layer B with codified test-quality rules cam learned empirically but never wrote down. (1) Anti-mock as a citable rubric line (warren CONSTITUTION Art. IV verbatim: 'a test that asserts a mock was called is documentation, not verification'); the reviewer FAILs a story that introduces new mock/fake/spy helpers or tests that skip real-dependency setup; codifies the CAM-55 fakes-lie lesson. (2) Adversarial-cases mandate: tests must cover malformed input, boundary values, and 'the case that broke last time', not happy-path only. (3) Per-test discipline checklist: behavior-named tests, one concept per test, async via a waitForCondition helper NOT a fixed setTimeout (anti-flake; this is the flaky_test_detection rubric gap and matches the reviewer suggestion about the hardcoded sleeps in tmux-introspect.test.ts), and a success/error/edge triad per feature. Written as reviewer-rubric items + a short AGENTS/CLAUDE convention ('real I/O, no mocks, mkdtemp, document why if you must mock'). Source: warren docs/CONSTITUTION.md Art. IV; kotadb testing_expert_review.md + testing_expert_plan.md; sapling/canopy/mulch/plot/seeds CONTRIBUTING 'no mocks' rule.

issues.title: Harden supervisor<->worker boundary: orchestrator-surface contract test + actor-ACL + empty-push verification
issues.description: Three boundary-hardening items, each mapping to a CAM-55/57-class bug. (1) Orchestrator-surface contract test (sapling orchestrator-surface.test.ts pattern): one test that pins the supervisor<->worker protocol shape (the send-keys submit form, the worker-report.json schema, the CAM_*_STATUS line, the @cam_label lifecycle) with a mock worker + real supervisor logic; would have caught the CAM-55 literal-Enter and CAM-57 dead-pane classes early. (2) Actor-ACL (plot src/acl.ts pattern): a worker actor must NOT be able to mutate its own acceptanceCriteria/goal or self-flip a story to passes:true; only the deterministic supervisor (after the reviewer verdict) or the operator can. A worker that disputes acceptance emits a blocker and halts. Hardens the two-layer against a worker gaming its own oracle. (3) Empty-push verification (warren ACCEPTANCE.md): branchPushed=true does not prove a commit (can fire on empty-push); gate on 'gh ... ahead_by >= 1' matching intent before treating a worker run as done. Source: sapling orchestrator-surface.test.ts; plot src/acl.ts; warren ACCEPTANCE.md / reap.empty_push.

issues.title: Typed pattern records + outcome-status + decay (mulch model), replacing free-text patterns.md
issues.description: cam's scripts/cam/patterns.md is free-text bullets with no structure, no outcome tracking, and no decay: a pattern that later proves wrong is never detected or demoted, and the file grows monotonically. Adopt the mulch expertise-record model: (1) typed records (schema-validated: type, classification tier foundational/tactical/observational, recorded_at, name/description, evidence, dir_anchors = the paths the pattern is about, outcomes[]); (2) outcome-status: append {status: success|failure|partial, recorded_at} whenever a pattern is applied (cam's supervisor/reviewer already produce pass/fail signals to wire in) + confirmation-scoring (successCount + 0.5*partialCount) so unconfirmed patterns sink; (3) decay/demotion as a gate: a cam prune that demotes superseded patterns one tier, archives stale tactical/observational by shelf-life (14d/30d), and (optionally) demotes patterns whose dir_anchors point at files that no longer exist (anchor-decay). This is real 'learning-capture as a gate'. Source: mulch src/schemas/record.ts, src/commands/prune.ts, src/utils/scoring.ts.

issues.title: Worker-pane closes on completion (kill-pane after report; CAM-57 recreates next dispatch)
issues.description:
After an implementer/reviewer worker finishes and pushes its report, the worker pane lingers (the claude TUI stays idle at its prompt) until the next dispatch respawns it. Dogfood 2026-06-16: US-004 emitted CAM_IMPLEMENTER_STATUS=DONE and wrote worker-report.json, but the pane stayed open. Desired: the supervisor closes (kill-pane) the worker pane as soon as it reads the completion report; CAM-57's ensureWorkerPane recreates a dead/missing pane on the next dispatch, so close-then-recreate is safe now. Two benefits: (1) clean UX, the worker pane exists only while a worker is actually active; (2) mutex consistency, closing returns the session to the canonical 2-pane idle state, so the 2-pane dispatch mutex reads idle instead of treating a lingering 3rd pane as busy. NOT CAM-58 (that is the loop false-terminal logic; this is the pane lifecycle). Acceptance sketch: after the completion-report is read (loop.ts implement branch + review.ts), kill-pane the worker pane; assert a completed worker leaves the session at 2 panes and the next dispatch recreates a titled worker pane. Builds on CAM-57 self-heal + CAM-55 mutex. Source: dogfood observation.

DEPENDENCIA (CAM-80, 2026-06-25): a frase "CAM-57 recreates ... so close-then-recreate is safe now" e incompleta GEOMETRICAMENTE. O recreate via openPaneInSession (session.ts:436) splita o pane ATIVO sem tamanho fixo (nao-deterministico, ver CAM-80), entao fechar o worker-pane a cada story faria o worker recriar em geometria aleatoria/pequena (49x24 inferior-direito) toda vez. CAM-80 (geometria deterministica do worker-pane) e PRE-REQUISITO deste: fazer CAM-80 antes ou junto, senao o CAM-65 piora a UX em vez de melhorar.

issues.title: Dashboard polish: truncate long story titles (list) + harden the Loop-header ghost
issues.description: Two cam dashboard render issues from dogfood 2026-06-16. (1) Story titles overflow: src/ui/Dashboard.tsx renders story.title raw (lines 562/573, no truncation), so long titles wrap and interleave with the per-story token counts, breaking the list layout. Fix (operator chose this approach): truncate the list row to a fixed width with a trailing ellipsis; the full title already shows in the detail subview (the navigable per-story view from CAM-50), so 'enter the story to read all' already works, no PRD schema change. (2) Loop-header ghosting: the 'Loop' section header stacks/duplicates on rapid terminal reflow (seen as many repeated 'Loop' lines). src/commands/dashboard.ts:837-848 already mitigates a single resize by clearing the alt-screen on the resize event, but it still ghosts under a reflow/dispatch storm (intermittent; clean in a later screenshot). Harden it (periodic full-clear, or fix the stale Ink line-count tracking at the old width). Both are pure src/ui/Dashboard.tsx + src/commands/dashboard.ts changes. Source: dogfood screenshots.

issues.title: cam stop must kill the sidecar + clean all markers; cam run abnormal-exit orphans the sidecar
issues.description: Dogfood 2026-06-17: after the operator closed the session and ran cam stop, an orphan cam sidecar process was still running (observed ~11h uptime, having survived multiple sessions; sidecars accumulate, consistent with the 'two sidecars alive ~15h' seen in the CAM-56 dogfood), plus stale markers left behind (.claude/.cam-orch-session, .claude/.cam-worker-pane, scripts/cam/worker-report.json). cam stop kills the tmux session but does NOT kill the sidecar process and does not clean all markers; and a cam run killed abnormally (session closed rather than a clean SIGINT/SIGTERM to the cam run process) orphans its sidecar (the sidecar only dies via cam run's own SIGINT/SIGTERM cleanup handler). Result: orphan sidecars poll forever and pile up across sessions. Fix: (1) cam stop locates and kills the project's sidecar (via the supervisor-lock recorded pid, or a scoped kill) and removes ALL per-session markers (.cam-orch-session, .cam-worker-pane, worker-report.json, .cam-supervisor.lock, cam-loop.local.md, .cam-orch-ready); (2) the sidecar self-terminates when its session is gone (poll for the tmux session and exit if absent within one idle interval) so an orphan can never poll indefinitely. Acceptance sketch: after cam stop, no cam sidecar process remains and all markers are gone; killing the cam run session without a clean stop leaves no orphan sidecar within one poll interval; a regression test on the cam stop teardown (lock-pid kill + marker cleanup) and on the sidecar session-absent self-exit. NOT CAM-58 (that is the loop false-terminal/outcome logic). Relates to the sidecar lifecycle (CAM-55 spawn, CAM-57 self-heal) and the memory note that active:false alone does not halt the sidecar. Source: dogfood observation.

issues.title: Gitignore os markers runtime do harness que escaparam (.cam-orchestrator-prompt.txt tracked + .cam-orch-ready + .cam-sidecar.pid): repo + template + teste
issues.description: Tres arquivos runtime do cam escaparam do .gitignore que ja cobre os irmaos (CAM-21/22/32/55), entao toda sessao cam run suja o working tree em qualquer branch (atrapalha o /cam-prune, que aborta em arvore suja). (1) .claude/.cam-orchestrator-prompt.txt e TRACKED no git mas reescrito por cam run a cada boot (src/commands/run.ts:318, writeFileSync(promptFile, buildOrchestratorBootPrompt())); a copia commitada fica stale (faltava o bloco do ready-marker US-FIX-005), entao aparece como 'M' em toda sessao. Nao e seed: e gerado de codigo (buildOrchestratorBootPrompt em run.ts:172), entao deve ser gitignored E removido do tracking (git rm --cached). (2) .claude/.cam-orch-ready (ORCH_READY_MARKER, src/tmux/bootstrap-wait.ts) e criado no boot do orquestrador mas nao esta no .gitignore (aparece como '??'); e irmao do .cam-orch-session, ja ignorado na linha 43 do .gitignore. (3) .claude/.cam-sidecar.pid (SIDECAR_PID_FILE, src/supervisor/sidecar-pid.ts, escrito por run.ts no spawn do sidecar) tambem nao esta ignorado. FIX (precedente CAM-49, consertar repo E produto): adicionar as 3 regras ao .gitignore deste repo E ao .gitignore que cam init materializa nos projetos do usuario (templates/ + regen de src/vendor/_generated.ts via bun run embed-vendor), git rm --cached no .cam-orchestrator-prompt.txt, e um teste no templatesContents map que pina as 3 regras e garante que o prompt-file nao volta a ser tracked. LATENTE (avaliar incluir no escopo): .cam-setup-menu.sh e .cam-setup-prompt.txt tem o mesmo defeito (tracked + reescritos por cam init) mas so sujam ao rodar cam init, nao toda sessao. Fonte: investigacao 2026-06-23 (varredura do src confirmou run.ts:318 + inventario completo de markers runtime sob .claude/).

issues.title: Smoke check-agent-frontmatter quebra com 'Missing default export' quando o cache global do Bun tem js-yaml ESM-only (5.x): resolucao nao-deterministica via auto-install em tmpdir
issues.description: REPRO 2026-06-23 (pre-flight do /cam-plan): 2 testes falham, test/init.test.ts 'writes config.toml with permission_mode=bypassPermissions on a fresh path' e 'preserves existing keys when re-running', ambos via cam init rodando o smoke vendored check-agent-frontmatter.ts. CAUSA-RAIZ (confirmada por probe runtime): o teste roda cam init num tmpdir (mkdtempSync, test/init.test.ts:26); init.ts:265 materializa e roda o smoke vendored nesse tmpdir, que NAO tem node_modules; o smoke faz 'import yaml from js-yaml' (default import; mesmo shape em src/commands/status.ts:43 e no blob checkAgentFrontmatterTsContents de src/vendor/_generated.ts); sem node_modules o Bun AUTO-INSTALA js-yaml pegando a versao mais alta do cache global; o cache do operador ganhou js-yaml@5.1.0 (alem de 4.1.1 e 4.2.0, de outro projeto), que e ESM com SO named exports (sem default), entao a importacao quebra com 'SyntaxError: Missing default export in module .../js-yaml@5.1.0/dist/js-yaml.mjs' e o smoke sai !=0, derrubando os 2 testes do init. cam-cli pina js-yaml@^4.1.1 (package.json/bun.lock/node_modules todos 4.1.1) entao DENTRO do repo passa; o bug so morde quando o smoke roda FORA do contexto do repo (o tmpdir do teste, ou um projeto-usuario sem js-yaml local) E o cache global tem uma versao ESM-only. Codigo intocado desde o CAM-67 (era 995/0); o que mudou foi so o cache global. IMPACTO PRODUTO: cam init num projeto de usuario sem js-yaml no node_modules e com js-yaml 5.x no cache global quebraria o check-agent-frontmatter do mesmo jeito (falso-negativo de smoke no setup). FIX (decidir no plan): (a) o smoke usa named import 'import { load } from js-yaml' em vez de default (validar que a versao alvo expoe o named load); (b) resolver js-yaml deterministicamente (rodar o smoke no contexto do repo com node_modules, ou embutir js-yaml no vendor, ou cravar a versao); ou (c) o smoke nao depender de js-yaml (parser de frontmatter YAML minimo, ja que so le name/description/model/tools). Espelhar no produto: templates/ + src/vendor/_generated.ts via bun run embed-vendor; avaliar o mesmo default-import em src/commands/status.ts:43 (roda no repo, nao morde hoje). RELACIONA: CAM-59 (CI verde-local==verde-no-CI; esta e exatamente a classe de bug que um CI limpo + ci-parity expoem). Fonte: pre-flight 2026-06-23 + probe runtime confirmando o auto-install pegar 5.1.0 num tmpdir.

issues.title: Reviewer verdict never reaches the orchestrator (it hangs at 'wait for review')
issues.description: Dogfood 2026-06-23: after the sidecar dispatched the reviewer and the reviewer emitted <review>CLEAN</review> in its pane, the orchestrator sat idle at 'wait for review' forever; the operator had to tell it manually. Root cause = an asymmetry between the implementer and reviewer completion paths. The implementer has an exit-report (US-003): it writes worker-report.json AND send-keys a one-line summary to the orchestrator pane, so the orchestrator narrates it. The reviewer has NO exit-report: it only emits the <review> tag, which the SIDECAR detects by polling capture-pane (review.ts), and the supervisor never send-keys anything to the orchestrator pane (getOrchPaneId is used only by the thin-proxy CLI commands, never by the supervisor loop). So the sidecar detects CLEAN, updates prd.review and reaches terminal, but nothing hands the verdict back to the orchestrator, which hangs. Incomplete CAM-55 conversion (push-on-exit was applied to the implementer, not the reviewer). Fix: give the reviewer the same exit-report push the implementer has (write a report + send-keys the verdict line to the orchestrator pane), OR have the sidecar push the terminal verdict to the orchestrator on review-done. Acceptance: after a reviewer emits CLEAN/FIXES_PENDING the orchestrator receives the verdict in its pane and narrates it WITHOUT the operator intervening; a contract/integration test pins the reviewer->orchestrator hand-back. Relates to CAM-63 (supervisor<->worker boundary), CAM-65 (worker-pane close). Prerequisite for CAM-71. Source: dogfood observation.

issues.title: End-to-end autonomy from plan-approval to ship (auto cam next + auto ship on CLEAN)
issues.description: Make the cycle fully autonomous AFTER the plan scope-approval, which stays the single human gate. Two manual touchpoints to auto-chain: (1) plan-approval -> auto-trigger the loop: at the end of cam-plan (Step 9, after the operator approves scope at Step 6 and the PRD/branch are committed) auto-flip active:true (the cam next trigger) instead of just printing 'run /cam-next'; (2) review-CLEAN -> auto-ship: when the sidecar reaches the review-CLEAN terminal state (all non-operator stories pass + review CLEAN) auto-trigger /cam-ship (gates + push + PR + close issue) instead of requiring a manual ship. The implement->review middle is already autonomous (sidecar + CAM-58 false-terminal fix). DEPENDS ON CAM-70: auto-ship needs the orchestrator to learn the CLEAN verdict (the reviewer/sidecar->orchestrator hand-back), since /cam-ship is LLM-driven (PR body) and runs in the orchestrator. Auto-ship is outward-facing (push + open PR), so it is an EXPLICIT opt-in behavior (default-on for the full-autonomy operator; a toggle can live in the cam config of CAM-53). Plan scope-approval remains the only place the loop waits for a human. Acceptance: after approving a plan, the cycle runs implement -> review -> ship with no further operator input, opening the PR on a CLEAN review; auto-ship is gated behind an explicit opt-in flag. Source: operator request 2026-06-23.

issues.title: Cycle-close hygiene do /cam-ship deve ser deterministico (src + teste), nao step de markdown executado pelo LLM: git rm recusa prd.json sujo (review block) mesmo com --ignore-unmatch
issues.description: DIRETRIZ RAIZ (operador, 2026-06-23): o cycle-close hygiene do ship NAO pode ser tarefa do LLM. Hoje o Step 4b vive em .claude/commands/cam-ship.md (e no template templates/commands/cam-ship.md) como markdown que o orquestrador executa a mao, entao uma sequencia git fragil (close backend + git rm do estado per-branch + commit) depende do LLM rodar exatamente certo. Falhou uma vez no proprio ship do CAM-68. FIX: mover o cycle-close inteiro pra CODIGO DETERMINISTICO em src/ (ex.: um primitivo `cam ship --finalize` ou finalizeCycleClose() chamado pelo ship) que (a) fecha o issue do backend local em issues.local.json, (b) remove o estado per-branch (prd.json, handoff.json) de forma robusta independente de sujo/ausente, (c) commita; o Step 4b do markdown vira UMA invocacao desse comando. BUG CONCRETO que motivou (pego no dogfood do ship do CAM-68): o Step 4b roda `git rm -q --ignore-unmatch scripts/cam/prd.json scripts/cam/handoff.json scripts/cam/progress.txt`. O CAM-49 adicionou --ignore-unmatch pra variante de pathspec inexistente, mas essa flag NAO sobrepoe o guard de 'local modifications'. No ship o prd.json carrega o review block escrito pelo supervisor (prd.review CLEAN, gravado DEPOIS do ultimo commit de story), entao esta sujo; o `git rm --ignore-unmatch` recusa ('local modifications'), o rm atomico aborta (leva o handoff.json junto, deixando-o tracked), e o `git add -A` seguinte re-commita o prd.json MODIFICADO em vez de remove-lo. Isso re-vaza estado per-branch pro main, derrotando o CAM-27 (o exato invariante que o CAM-49 protege). Pego a mao via git show --stat + git ls-files e consertado in-cycle com `git rm -f --ignore-unmatch` + commit --amend antes do push. O codigo deterministico deve resolver o caso sujo (force, ou stage-then-rm, ou commitar o review block primeiro) e o ausente (ignore-unmatch), os dois. TESTE: reproduzir a forma do prd.json sujo (review block nao-commitado) e asseverar que prd.json + handoff.json terminam DELETADOS, nao modificados. Se o markdown ficar no template, espelhar e regenerar src/vendor/_generated.ts (embed-vendor). Relaciona: CAM-49 (variante pathspec-inexistente, closed), CAM-27 (invariante defendido), CAM-71 (auto-ship depende desse fechamento ser deterministico e correto). Prioridade P1: falha silenciosa que re-vaza estado per-branch pro main; existe workaround manual (orquestrador verifica + amenda) mas e invisivel sem ele, e a diretriz e remover o LLM do caminho.

issues.title: Habilitar branch protection (required status checks) na main agora que o repo e publico + CI existe; corrigir a premissa 'free private plan' em docs/agent-readiness.md
issues.description: ACHADO (dogfood do CAM-59, PR #65): o repo cam-cli e PUBLICO (gh api repos/.../  private:false), nao private. O CAM-59 e o docs/agent-readiness.md assumiram que branch protection era um 'structural fail of the free private plan' (linhas 25 e 33-34 do doc: 'branch_protection blocked (free private plan)' e 'branch_protection as a structural fail of the free private plan'), e a nota do proprio CAM-59 dizia 'hard merge-block via branch protection is unavailable on the free private plan'. Premissa errada: repo publico tem branch protection + required status checks de graca. ESCOPO: (a) corrigir docs/agent-readiness.md: branch_protection deixa de ser impossibilidade estrutural e vira um gap fechavel; reavaliar a contagem da linha 'Development Workflow' e a nota de judgment-call (linhas 32-34). (b) Habilitar required-status-checks branch protection na main exigindo o check de CI do CAM-59 (gh api repos/eduardocaminha/cam-cli/branches/main/protection ou via UI), agora que a CI existe e o merge-block e de fato possivel. CONTEXTO: o CAM-59 entregou o sinal + ci-parity dizendo explicitamente que o merge-block estava fora de alcance; o CAM-73 destrava o merge-block real. Passa pelo loop + review normal. Relaciona: CAM-59 (CI keystone, entregou o check), CAM-49/CAM-27 (invariantes de estado per-branch).

issues.title: cam issue list: comando de CLI deterministico que lista os issues locais no terminal (backend none); linear/github usam a UI nativa
issues.description: PEDIDO (operador, 2026-06-24): um comando de CLI que liste os issues no terminal, especifico pro backend LOCAL (issue_system = 'none'). Linear e GitHub NAO precisam: ja tem UI propria (app do Linear, web do GitHub / `gh issue list`); so o backend local fica sem jeito de ver a lista fora de uma sessao. SITUACAO ATUAL: `cam issue` (src/commands/issue.ts, runIssue) so implementa o caminho `create`, um thin-proxy que injeta `/cam-issue create <text>` no pane do orquestrador via send-keys, e parseIssueArgs (index.ts:454+) EXIGE um argumento de texto-livre (erra sem ele). Listar issues so existe via `/cam-issue list` (slash, .claude/commands/cam-issue.md secao `none`), que roda DENTRO de uma sessao claude e e renderizado pelo LLM: precisa do orquestrador vivo, nao da output deterministico e nao serve pra um glance rapido do terminal. PEDIDO CONCRETO: um `cam issue list` (ou `cam issues`) DETERMINISTICO que le scripts/cam/issues.local.json direto e renderiza os issues open como tabela no terminal, SEM spawnar claude e SEM passar pelo pane do orquestrador. Mesma familia read-only deterministica de `cam status` / `cam dashboard` (que ja leem prd.json/state direto via src/commands/status.ts). ESCOPO/PONTEIROS: (a) parseIssueArgs em index.ts deixa de exigir texto-livre e passa a reconhecer o subcomando `list` (sem quebrar `cam issue "<texto>"` = create); (b) um runIssueList (ou ramo em runIssue) em src/commands/issue.ts que le issue_system de scripts/cam/project.toml (reusar src/config/toml.ts) e, no caso `none`, le e renderiza issues.local.json; (c) renderizar com os helpers de src/logging/ (tabela: id, priority, state, titulo truncado), sem Ink, no print-path linear; (d) testes em test/ (parse do subcomando + render de uma fixture de issues.local.json). DECIDIR NO PLANO: nome final (`cam issue list` vs `cam issues`); filtro default (so open? flag --all/--state para closed); ordenacao (priority desc, tie-break id asc, espelhando a regra de prioridade do CAM-25); e o comportamento pros backends nao-locais: ou imprime um hint curto apontando pra UI nativa (`gh issue list` / app do Linear) ou nao oferece o `list` (decisao do operador: linear/github nao precisam). Relaciona: CAM-25 (token canonico de issue + regra de prioridade local), CAM-11 (cam issue como subcomando de CLI / caminho create). Prioridade P2: ergonomia de operador util no dia a dia, escopo pequeno e deterministico.

issues.title: Reviewer findings nao propagam pras fix stories (US-R*-001): o fix-worker recebe prompt generico, re-deriva o finding e no-opa
issues.description:
ACHADO (dogfood do CAM-53, PR #68): quando o reviewer devolve FIXES_PENDING:N, o supervisor auto-gera N fix stories placeholder (US-R<round>-001..00N) contendo SO { id, title: '...address reviewer finding', priority, passes:false }, SEM description nem acceptanceCriteria. O fix-worker e entao dispatchado com o prompt generico 'Implement the next user story from scripts/cam/prd.json per your AGENT.md' e NENHUM texto do finding, entao tem que re-derivar o que o reviewer flagou lendo o subagent-reviewer.md e re-revisando, o que e nao-confiavel: no CAM-53 o US-R2-001 saiu code no-op (mexeu so em prd.json/handoff.json/patterns.md+1 linha) e o MESMO finding reincidiu no round 3; o review nao convergiu em 3 rounds (3->1->1) e exigiu fix manual do operador. Os findings CRITICAL/WARNING do reviewer (com evidencia citada por file:line) vivem SO no pane/transcript do reviewer; o sidecar parseia o <review> APENAS pro contador do verdict (parseReviewVerdict), nao persiste os findings na fix story nem no task prompt do fix-worker. FIX: propagar os findings do reviewer pro caminho de fix. Opcoes: (a) o sidecar captura o bloco de findings do output do reviewer e escreve na description/notes da fix story (ou num artifact de findings que o fix-worker le); (b) o task prompt do fix-worker inclui os findings verbatim. Mesma classe de CAM-58/CAM-70 (handback estruturado em vez de pane-scraping). ONDE: o dispatch de review-fix em src/supervisor/ (o caminho que cria as US-R<round>-001 e dispatcha o fix-worker), a captura do output do reviewer (o parse do <review> ja extrai o verdict; estender pra capturar os findings), e a construcao do task prompt / worker-argv. ACEITE: um fix-worker dispatchado pro round N recebe os findings exatos do reviewer (na description ou no task prompt), nao um placeholder generico 'address reviewer finding'; regressao que asseria que o texto do finding chega na fix story / prompt. Prioridade P1: torna o loop de review autonomo nao-confiavel; reproduziu live no CAM-53 forcando intervencao manual. Relaciona: CAM-56 (two-layer verification), CAM-58/CAM-70 (handback estruturado), CAM-76 (cap de maxRounds, mesmo dogfood).

UPDATE 2026-06-25 (decisao do operador, reframe pos-dogfood): o dogfood live de US-007 PROVOU que a abordagem do US-001 (parseReviewFindings sobre capture-pane) NAO funciona: o capture-pane devolve o markdown JA RENDERIZADO pela TUI (os ## e - sao consumidos pelo renderer e somem), entao o parser extrai 0 findings e cai no placeholder (graceful degradation US-005). A tag <review> sobrevive (nao e markdown) entao o verdict parseia, mas os findings nao. NOVA ABORDAGEM (handback estruturado, alinhado a intencao original "estruturado, nao pane-scraping"): o subagent-reviewer ESCREVE review-report.json {verdict, findings:[{severity,file,line,text}]}; o sidecar LE esse arquivo pra verdict E findings; deleta parseReviewFindings-on-pane e para de parsear a tag <review> pra controle (mantem como sentinel humano). Salva US-002/004/005/006 adaptados pra ler do report. ALEM disso, corrigir os 2 findings reais que o reviewer pegou: (CRITICAL) host.ts:320-359 nao pluga findingsArtifactWriter (artifact nunca escrito em producao, classe CAM-53); (WARNING) recovery-runbook drift (shape {severity,file,line,text}, findings->findingsCount, round->roundsCompleted, placeholder text). Primeira fatia da unificacao de comunicacao inter-pane (ver CAM-77/CAM-78). Re-plan necessario.

issues.title: maxRounds nao e terminal duro: o loop dispatcha um (maxRounds+1)-esimo fix em vez de declarar MAX_ROUNDS_DEBT
issues.description: ACHADO (dogfood do CAM-53, PR #68): o review chegou em roundsCompleted:3 com maxRounds:3 e lastVerdict FIXES_PENDING:1, mas o supervisor AINDA dispatchou uma 4a fix story (US-R3-001) em vez de converter pro estado terminal MAX_ROUNDS_DEBT. Por scripts/cam/CLAUDE.md o review e terminal quando lastVerdict === 'CLEAN' OU 'MAX_ROUNDS_DEBT'; o cap existe justamente pra estancar um review que nao converge (o whack-a-mole exato que o CAM-53 sofreu, agravado pelo CAM-75: o fix-worker nao recebe o finding e no-opa). O loop em vez disso seguiu gerando fix rounds (R1, R2, R3, indo pro R4) e teria spinado indefinidamente se o operador nao tivesse dado soft-pause (active:false). FIX: enforce maxRounds como terminal DURO: quando um round de review devolve FIXES_PENDING e roundsCompleted >= maxRounds, setar lastVerdict = 'MAX_ROUNDS_DEBT' (terminal) e NAO dispatchar outro fix round; o loop entao sai awaiting-operator/complete-with-debt e o finding restante vira debito documentado. ONDE: a logica de review-round em src/supervisor/loop.ts (o branch que incrementa roundsCompleted e decide dispatchar fixes vs terminar). ACEITE: com maxRounds:N, um review ainda FIXES_PENDING depois de N rounds seta MAX_ROUNDS_DEBT e o supervisor alcanca um estado terminal SEM dispatchar um (N+1)-esimo fix; teste de regressao no supervisor. Prioridade P2: cap de seguranca; o operador tem o workaround de soft-pause, mas o loop deveria auto-terminar. Relaciona: CAM-53 (reproduziu live), CAM-56 (rounds de two-layer verification), CAM-75 (causa-raiz do nao-convergir, mesmo dogfood).

issues.title: Unificar canal do implementer em worker-report.json (fonte unica de outcome); handoff vira so contexto-pra-frente; colapsar cross-check do readWorkerOutcome
issues.description: Parte 2 da unificacao de comunicacao inter-pane (decisao 2026-06-25, ver CAM-75/CAM-78). Canal do implementer: tornar worker-report.json a UNICA fonte autoritativa de outcome do sidecar (outcome+story+gates), tirando handoff.json do caminho de outcome (handoff vira SO contexto-pra-frente do proximo agente, duravel/commitado; nunca sinal de controle do sidecar). Demote o sentinel CAM_IMPLEMENTER_STATUS a humano-legivel (nao parseado como gate). Completion-detect via watch do worker-report.json (mantem pane-died + timeout como redes de FALHA, legitimas). Colapsa o cross-check de 3 fontes do readWorkerOutcome (result.ts ~268-424: sentinel + handoff + report) num read autoritativo do report + confirmacao de integridade contra prd.json passes (evento-vs-estado, NAO double-push). Espelha o padrao de report estruturado que o CAM-75 pilota pro reviewer. ONDE: src/supervisor/result.ts (readWorkerOutcome), src/supervisor/loop.ts (poll loop, parseAnySentinel), .claude/agents/subagent-implementer.md (sentinel deixa de ser gate). Modelo de 5 concerns: Evento=worker-report.json, Estado=prd.json, Contexto=handoff.json, Observabilidade=cam-worker-events.jsonl, Sabedoria=patterns.md. Depende do CAM-75 (pilota o padrao).

issues.title: /cam-ship roda o check:all completo (nao so typecheck+tests): ship verde garante CI verde, fim do green-local != green-CI pos-ship
issues.description: RECORRENTE (CAM-53/59/60, de novo no CAM-75 PR #69): a CI fica VERMELHA logo apos o orquestrador declarar shipped. Causa: o /cam-ship Step 3 roda so `bun run typecheck` + `bun test` + `bun run embed-vendor:check`, enquanto a CI roda `bun run check:all` (o gate spine completo: typecheck, test, embed-vendor, biome/lint, file-size ratchet, debt-markers, coverage ratchet, knip dead-code, jscpd dup, ci-parity). O worker per-story TAMBEM roda so typecheck+tests, entao crescimento de arquivo (file-size ratchet), queda de cobertura, dup, dead-code etc. acumulam silenciosos e so estouram no CI. No CAM-75, 4 arquivos passaram do teto (review.ts/test, decide.ts, host.ts) e a 1a CI ficou vermelha pos-ship. FIX: o /cam-ship Step 3 passa a rodar `bun run check:all` (exatamente o que a CI roda; o gate ci-parity do CAM-59 ja garante manifest local == CI), substituindo a forma parcial typecheck+test+embed. Assim ship verde => CI verde por construcao. Quando o check:all falhar no ship por crescimento legitimo (ratchet), o ship FALHA com mensagem clara e o operador/worker sobe o teto em file-size-budget.json (ou o floor em coverage-budget.json) com o _ref do issue ANTES de abrir o PR. ONDE: .claude/commands/cam-ship.md Step 3 + templates/commands/cam-ship.md espelhado + regen embed (src/vendor/_generated.ts, embed-vendor:check), e uma regressao no test do templatesContents embarcado que pina check:all no Step 3 e proibe a forma parcial isolada. AVALIAR (fora do MVP): rodar check:all tambem no pre-flight do /cam-plan e /cam-next (mais pesado, ~30-60s; o ratchet e cumulativo, faz mais sentido no ship). Tambem avaliar um teto/limite que faca o worker per-story ao menos AVISAR de crescimento. Prioridade P1: higiene recorrente que custa um ciclo de CI vermelho + retrabalho a cada ship; o operador pediu explicitamente o fix definitivo (nunca mais).

issues.title: Geometria deterministica do worker-pane: openPaneInSession splita pane explicito (orquestrador) com tamanho fixo, nao o pane ativo (session:0 -v). Pre-req do CAM-65
issues.description: Bug latente exposto no dogfood do CAM-75 (2026-06-25): o worker-pane (implementer/reviewer reusado) nasce de openPaneInSession (src/tmux/session.ts:436-449) via `split-window -t <session>:0 -v -d ... cat` SEM `-t <pane>` explicito e SEM flags de tamanho, entao o tmux divide o pane ATIVO 50/50. Normalmente o orquestrador e o pane ativo no 1o dispatch, entao o worker nasce largo abaixo do orquestrador e e reusado (respawn-pane -k, mesmo id). MAS quando o pane morre e o self-heal (CAM-57, host.ts:300-317 ensureWorkerPaneFn) recria com a DASHBOARD (coluna direita ~49 col) ativa, o worker nasce 49x24 no canto inferior-direito, ilegivel pro output do reviewer/implementer (que despejam mais texto que o orquestrador). Confirmado no runtime: reviewer pane=%5 (recriado ~4x por kills manuais), 49x24 @139,26, filho do split da coluna direita; o orquestrador (138x49) intocado. FIX: openPaneInSession deve mirar um pane EXPLICITO (o orchestrator pane id, ou criar na coluna/posicao canonica) com TAMANHO EXPLICITO (-l/-x/-y), deterministico em create E recreate, independente de qual pane esta ativo; opcionalmente normalizar via select-layout/resize-pane pos-create (o hook window-resized do CAM-48 so re-clampa a dashboard, nunca o worker). Considerar dar ao worker espaco proeminente. DEPENDENCIA CRITICA com CAM-65: o CAM-65 fecha o worker-pane quando ocioso, o que torna TODO dispatch um recreate; sem o CAM-80 o CAM-65 faria a geometria aleatoria/pequena acontecer em CADA story (nao so apos kills manuais). Logo CAM-80 e PRE-REQUISITO do CAM-65: sequenciar CAM-80 antes, ou os dois juntos. ONDE: src/tmux/session.ts:436-449 (openPaneInSession), src/supervisor/host.ts:300-317 (ensureWorkerPaneFn), src/tmux/session.ts:389-401 (window-resized hook, hoje so dashboard). Prioridade P2 (UX do cam run + pre-req do CAM-65). Descoberto verificando o runtime (a leitura estatica sozinha previu worker largo; o runtime revelou o split do pane ativo).
